project.title: Iris dataset exploration
project.alt: Working Iris observation explorer with native species and feature controls, actual source points and checked summary cards
project.desc: Filter species, compare any pair of Iris measurements and inspect the original rows behind independently checked summaries.
project.built: Built an interactive observation lab over the preserved 150-row analysis, with species filters, four-feature selectors, exact source tables and filtered CSV downloads.
project.why: Before choosing a model, it helps to see how measurements vary and which features reveal useful structure. Clear exploratory analysis makes a dataset easier to understand.
how: Choose observed species and any horizontal/vertical feature; axis ranges stay fixed as species change.
Compare browser-computed means and sample SD with independent Python reference summaries.
Inspect every selected source row or download all four original measurements and supplied species labels.
project.demonstrates: Data provenance, descriptive statistics, independent numerical checks, accessible interactive graphics and reproducible publication.
project.caption: Actual working explorer: original observations use species-specific shapes and colours; summary cards show sample means and SD in centimetres.
project.result: Generated from the same source analysis as the figures.
project.limits: This is descriptive exploration of a small, familiar teaching dataset. Separation in these observations is not independent validation of a classifier or evidence of general performance. Pooled correlations mix species and do not establish causation. Identical measurement rows are retained because equality alone does not prove duplicate sampling. The supplied CSV is preserved; historical Iris variants differ in two documented observations.
project.technical: The original analysis now also exports every source row and twelve reference summaries. Five Python regressions reconcile original rows, historical variants, provenance and statistics; two Node checks cover sample SD and CSV semantics; three browser journeys cover all sixteen feature pairings, filters, exports, failed loading and narrow layouts. Generated build metadata stays untracked. Original coursework and data remain intact.
project.run: Install requirements.txt; run python explore_iris.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v and python build_explorer.py. Run npm ci, npm run test:rules, npx playwright install chromium and npm run test:browser. Serve docs locally to explore.
gallery: A real species-filtered view; fifty supplied Virginica observations, with unchanged feature axes.
The same species controls, plots and summaries on a narrow screen.
Original petal and sepal figures retained alongside the interactive lab.
Every original measurement, with median/quartile boxes.
Species means plus/minus one sample SD, not confidence intervals.
project.challenge: Filtering must change the view without changing the evidence. The browser computes summaries independently, while Python exports reference statistics from the preserved source. Every feature pair is checked, repeated rows retain their original order, and the source hash and documented variant travel with the release.
